title: Sola fide does not deny causes outside us—mercy, merit, word, sacraments
source_text: XXVI. Et primo quidem hic observandum est, quum justificationem soli fidei ascribimus, per id nos non negare, quin justificatio, praeter fidem quae ad eam ex parte nostra requiritur, multas causas extra nos habeat, sive principales, ut Dei misericordiam, & Christi meritum; sive instrumentales, ut Evangelii verbum & Sacramenta. Itaque per istud solum significamus, intra nos, & ex parte nostra, unam fidem esse per quam justificemur. Adeo ut fides hic opponatur solis operibus: nec per hoc aliud intelligi, quam fidem justificare, opera vero minime.
pass_a_gloss: And first it must be observed here that when we ascribe justification to faith alone, by that we do not deny that justification, besides the faith required for it on our part, has many causes outside us—whether principal, as God's mercy and Christ's merit; or instrumental, as the word of the Gospel and the sacraments. Therefore by that alone we signify that within us, and on our part, there is one faith through which we are justified. So that faith here is opposed only to works: nor is anything else to be understood by this than that faith justifies, but works not at all.
pass_b_english: Sola fide does not deny mercy, Christ's merit, word, or sacraments as causes outside us.
On our part, only faith justifies—opposed to works, not to gospel means.

choices.why: Our-side instrument vs works—not denying Christ's merit.
